item.title: On Raku and Release
item.description: I am a potter. Through pottery, I have discovered not just an art form, but also a connection to creation and the Creator. Recently, I was given the opportunity to practice a new technique: Raku firing. Raku, known for its captivating rapid-firing and its ceremonial act of removing each piece while still in a blazing molten red-orange glow, has taught me so much about healing, control, release, endings, and transformation. item.title: Home no More: Chronicles from Pioneer Camp Alumni
item.description: From the Summer 2017 Issue Credit: Nicki Dugan Pogue Elle Dhanani met God at summer camp. A victim of intense bullying at school, she felt “camp was home.” It was where she found community and where she felt whole. This past summer, however, all of that unraveled. “I’ve always struggled with my sexuality,” says Dhanani. “I never really knew where I was on the spectrum until this past year. I hadn’t come out to my parents or any of my friends. Camp was the first place I came out.” Ontario Pioneer
